content.text:
I've submitted **index 22** (Bi 0.43, Fe 0.16, V 0.41) as the best composition. Its photocurrent was 5.3e-7 A, the highest of the three I measured. I can't say whether it's the best in the library: with only 3 merit measurements, most of the composition space was never tested.

| Index | Bi / Fe / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 22 | 0.43 / 0.16 / 0.41 | **5.3e-7 A** |
| 61 | 0.39 / 0.20 / 0.41 | 2.0e-7 A |
| 71 | 0.49 / 0.16 / 0.35 | 1.5e-7 A |

- **Why I started there:** BiVO₄ is the known light-active phase in the Bi-Fe-V oxide system, and it absorbs at the 2.4 eV used here. So I aimed at compositions near 1:1 Bi:V with little Fe.
- **XRD (4 of 5 used, on 22, 61, 79 and 88):** all four show BiVO₄ as the main phase, with its strongest peak at Q ≈ 2.04 Å⁻¹. Patterns 61 and 79 have a few minor peaks that 22 and 88 lack, which may be a slightly different secondary phase.
- **Trend:** more Fe (61) roughly halved the photocurrent. Moving to the Bi-rich, V-poor side (71) lowered it even more. Both point back to near-1:1 Bi:V with the least Fe the library offers (about 0.16).

I didn't measure 88 or 79 because they have more Fe than 22, which the result for 61 suggests is harmful.
